claims.claim: The functional and the cycle-accurate model reproduce all 22,000 expected words of the 9 golden vector sets.

The Verilog RTL (behavioural and carry-save/Kogge-Stone adder styles), the HLS kernels (C simulation with the stand-in and with the official ap_int headers) and the MATLAB/Octave model reproduce the same words.
One sample in and one coefficient out per clock, in natural order; first output after 16 clocks (8-point) and 97 clocks (8x8).
claims.evidence: cycle-accurate models; RTL and HLS test benches check the latency

claims.claim: 12 butterflies and 5 rotations per block; butterfly unit 75.0 % and CORDIC unit 62.5 % busy; 19 memory words; every value lives at most 8 cycles, so all addresses are functions of the 3-bit phase.

No node and no CORDIC register leaves its range in any of the 120 configurations (W = 8..16, every valid safe-scaling choice, both modes). Each is scanned with 69,536 inputs: the 65,536 near-corner inputs {-128, -127, 126, 127}^8 and 4,000 random ones. In every configuration the tightest node reaches its limit exactly; with the input alignment one bit too high the same scan flags 18 of 42 nodes.
1-D SQNR (20,000 random 8-bit vectors): Table 1 micro-rotations 45.72 dB at W = 14 and 45.72 dB at W = 16; CORDIC-II unit 69.63 dB at W = 14 and 71.68 dB at W = 16.

The plateau is the angle and gain error of the rotation set. Run with the realised rotation coefficients in floating point, the flow graph gives 45.72 dB (Table 1), which the fixed-point curve meets from W = 14, and 71.86 dB (CORDIC-II), 0.18 dB above the fixed-point value at W = 16. Largest angle error: 5.68e-03 rad (Table 1), 3.54e-04 rad (CORDIC-II).
2-D PSNR against the double-precision DCT at W = 14: 67.5 dB (Table 1), 72.2 dB (CORDIC-II); mean over 8 test images.
Zonal compression through the bit-accurate 2-D processor (W 14/16, Table 1) stays within 0.0014 dB of the double-precision DCT for every image and ratio (64:10, 64:6, 64:3, 64:1).

Paper Table 3 (BSD-100, WL 8..16) gives its ten rows (nine methods and the proposed one) within 1.08 dB of each other at every WL, so its PSNR follows the word length (6.3 dB per bit for the proposed row); the format of that word is not stated in the paper. On this repository's word-length scale the same PSNR is reached 4.5 to 4.7 bits earlier (interpolated at WL 16 and 14).
Zero multipliers; two-input adders at W = 14: 22 (Table 1), 28 (CORDIC-II). Counted from the RTL structure, not synthesised.
The 16-point extension (two 8-point processors and a CORDIC array with the paper's Table 5 constants) has rms error 0.45 (Table 1) and 0.248 (CORDIC-II) against the double-precision DCT.
FPGA figures of the paper (Artix-7 XC7A25T, Vivado 2018, WL 14): 0 DSP, 352 LUT, 440 FF, 144 Msps, 91 mW.
